method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the Australian Asthma Handbook v3.0 treatment-levels page. Dose bands transcribed from the source table and checked value by value.
source_coverage: Treatment levels page retrieved in full. Diagnosis, initial treatment, adjusting treatment, acute asthma and paediatric pages NOT retrieved.

claims.claim: All treatment levels include ICS; treatment solely with as-needed SABA is not recommended for adults or adolescents even if symptoms are infrequent
claims.source_text: All treatment levels include ICS. Treatment solely with as-needed SABA is not recommended for adults or adolescents with asthma, even if symptoms are infrequent.

claims.claim: Four treatment levels, least to most intensive; optimal level may change over time
claims.source_text: There are four levels of treatment, from least intensive to most intensive. ... The optimal step for an individual may change over time.

claims.claim: Level 1 recommended: low-dose budesonide-formoterol taken as needed (AIR-only)
claims.source_text: Level 1. Low-dose budesonide–formoterol, taken as needed (AIR-only)

claims.claim: Level 2 recommended: low-dose MART, maintenance low-dose ICS-formoterol plus extra doses from same inhaler as needed
claims.source_text: Level 2. Low-dose MART: maintenance treatment with a low dose of ICS-formoterol, plus extra doses from same inhaler taken as needed for relief of symptoms

claims.claim: Level 3 recommended: medium-dose MART using higher number of inhalations of the low-dose inhaler
claims.source_text: Level 3. Medium-dose MART: maintenance treatment with a medium dose of ICS-formoterol (higher number of inhalations using low-dose inhaler), plus extra doses from same inhaler taken as needed

claims.claim: Level 4: targeted intensive treatment based on ICS-LABA, sometimes with LAMAs or monoclonal antibodies
claims.source_text: Level 4. Targeted intensive treatment – more intensive regimens based on ICS-LABA, sometimes with add-on treatments such as LAMAs or monoclonal antibody therapies.

claims.claim: Alternatives at levels 1-3 pair maintenance ICS or ICS-LABA with as-needed SABA
claims.source_text: Level 1: maintenance treatment with a low dose of ICS, plus SABA taken as needed ... Level 2: maintenance treatment with a low dose of ICS-LABA, plus SABA ... Level 3: maintenance treatment with a medium dose of ICS-LABA, plus SABA taken as needed

claims.claim: Other ICS-LABA combinations cannot be used as MART
claims.source_text: Other combinations of an inhaled corticosteroid and a long-acting beta2 agonist cannot be used this way.

claims.claim: ICS-formoterol reliever regimens reduce severe exacerbations requiring OCS compared with as-needed SABA at levels 1-3; budesonide-formoterol as needed markedly reduces that risk vs SABA alone
claims.source_text: At treatment levels 1–3, these regimens reduce the risk of severe exacerbations requiring oral corticosteroids, compared with regimens using as-needed SABA for symptom relief: low-dose budesonide–formoterol taken as needed (without maintenance treatment) markedly reduces the risk of severe exacerbations requiring oral corticosteroids, compared with SABA alone.[Crossingham 2021]

claims.claim: MART reduces severe exacerbations requiring OCS compared with the same or higher dose of ICS or ICS-LABA
claims.source_text: Maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) with ICS-formoterol reduces the risk of severe exacerbations requiring OCS, compared with the same or higher dose of ICS or ICS-LABA.[Sobieraj 2018]

claims.claim: Short courses of OCS associated with increased lifetime risk of osteoporosis, pneumonia, cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, cataract, sleep apnoea, renal impairment, depression/anxiety, type 2 diabetes and weight gain
claims.source_text: Short courses of oral corticosteroids to manage asthma exacerbations are associated with increased lifetime risk of osteoporosis, pneumonia, cardiovascular or cerebrovascular diseases, cataract, sleep apnoea, renal impairment, depression/anxiety, type 2 diabetes, and weight gain. [Price 2018]

claims.claim: Poor ICS adherence is common; combining ICS with the reliever ensures ICS use at least when symptomatic
claims.source_text: Poor adherence to ICS is common. Combining ICS with symptom reliever ensures that patients use ICS, at least whenever they have symptoms.[Murphy 2021]

claims.claim: ICS dose bands: budesonide 200-400 low, 500-800 medium, >800 high; fluticasone propionate 100-200 / 250-500 / >500; ciclesonide 80-160 / 240-320 / >320; beclometasone extra-fine 100-200 / 250-400 / >400; fluticasone furoate - / 100 / 200
claims.source_text: Beclometasone dipropionate (extra-fine particle) | 100–200 | 250–400 | >400 | Budesonide | 200–400 | 500–800 | >800 | Ciclesonide | 80–160 | 240–320 | >320 | Fluticasone furoate | – | 100 | 200 | Fluticasone propionate | 100–200 | 250–500 | >500

claims.claim: The dose table does not indicate dose equivalence
claims.source_text: The table shows options for low, medium and high doses of each available inhaled corticosteroid (with or without LABA and LAMA) – it does not indicate dose equivalence.

claims.claim: Mometasone furoate doses shown as delivered dose, not metered dose; all others metered
claims.source_text: *Doses of mometasone furoate are shown as delivered dose (not metered dose) in line with inhaler labels. For all other products in this table, the inhaler label and table show the metered dose.

claims.claim: Montelukast carries a TGA warning about neuropsychiatric adverse effects; may be considered as add-on in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease; limited use in severe asthma
claims.source_text: Montelukast | May be considered as add-on treatment for patients with aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. Limited use in severe asthma. Montelukast TGA-approved product information and consumer medicine information carry a warning about potential neuropsychiatric adverse effects

claims.claim: Azithromycin is a specialist-care add-on for persistent exacerbations despite medium-dose ICS-LABA; screening required
claims.source_text: Azithromycin | An add-on treatment option used in specialist care for patients with persistent exacerbations despite maintenance treatment with medium-dose ICS-LABA. Screening is required and cautions apply

claims.claim: Patient must not be on a concomitant single-agent long-acting beta2 agonist
claims.source_text: Patient must not be on a concomitant single agent long-acting beta2 agonist.

claims.claim: A 3-day period of deteriorating symptoms after additional as-needed inhalations should prompt reassessment for alternative explanations
claims.source_text: If the patient experiences a 3-day period of deteriorating symptoms after taking additional as needed inhalations, the patient should be reassessed for alternative explanations of persisting symptoms.

claims.claim: Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 DPI maximum: 6 inhalations per occasion, 8 per day, 12 in one day temporarily; maxima rarely needed in practice
claims.source_text: 6 per occasion / 8 per day / 12 in one day temporarily ... Maximum doses as stated in TGA-approved product information (daily maximum rarely needed in practice)

claims.claim: AIR products carry 2 repeats; MART products carry 5 repeats; some MART listings flagged as 60-day prescribing requiring stable condition
claims.source_text: Maximum quantity (2 repeats for all) ... Maximum quantity (5 repeats for all) ... † Condition must be stable for the prescriber to consider the listed maximum quantity of this medicine suitable for this patient (60-day prescribing)

claims.claim: Age restrictions: most budesonide-formoterol products >=12 years; DuoResp Spiromax and Fostair >=18 years
claims.source_text: DuoResp Spiromax | DPI | 200/6 | >= 18 years ... Fostair (pMDI) | 100/6 | ... | 18 years ... Symbicort Rapihaler ... >= 12 years
